title: Rollout playbook: circuit-breakers and credit policy for legacy stream removal
creator: Leah Martinez
description: PRD for coordinated removal of legacy streaming endpoints (SSE/socket) focusing on circuit-breakers, customer opt-in grace period, and SLA credit/billing reconciliation. This doc captures goals, constraints, migration support, and acceptance criteria for a reversible rollout with automatic fallbacks.
problem_statement: Multiple clients still use legacy streaming transports that complicate runtime maintenance, increase operational cost, and limit improvements. Previous deprecation attempts caused outages for a subset of customers due to silent client failures and lack of clear billing adjustments for partial failures.
goals: Provide a staged, reversible rollout for legacy stream removal
Implement server-side circuit-breakers to auto-detect post-migration client failures and route to compatibility shim
Establish clear SLA credit rules for customer-impacting failures during migration windows
Deliver SDK and HTTP guidance plus automated telemetry gates to track readiness
non_goals: Force immediate client upgrades outside opt-in windows
Replace existing billing system or wholesale invoicing changes
requirements: Server: circuit-breaker per-customer and per-route with configurable thresholds
Console: per-customer migration toggle and credit calculation preview
Billing: automated detection of migration-induced errors with one-click credit reconciliation
SDKs: backoff guidance, connection diagnostics, and opt-in header flag
Telemetry: readiness gates (error-rate, reconnects, latency) exposed as dashboard and alert
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (announcement): 8-week notice to customers and public docs
Phase 1 (opt-in): 4-week opt-in window where customers can request early cutover
Phase 2 (canary): route 5% traffic to new path for selected customers with circuit-breaker monitoring
Phase 3 (ramp): increase to 25%, 50%, 100% with gates at each step
Phase 4 (enforced with opt-out): automatic fallback disabled after 4 weeks unless SLA tickets exist
rollback_policy: Circuit-breaker triggers immediate reroute to legacy compatibility shim for affected customers
Manual rollback via console toggle if systemic issues detected
Billing stop-gap: halt credit computation until postmortem if anomalies in detection appear
acceptance_criteria: Server-side circuit-breaker is tested and enabled in staging and dedicated clusters
Console shows per-customer migration status and allows manual fallback
Billing detection flagged >=90% of induced streaming errors in a controlled canary test
SDK guidance published and embedded in migration center
Runbook for SRE and Support documented and reviewed
client_guidance: Recommended SDK versions and minimums for auto-reconnect behavior
Sample retry/backoff pseudocode for longpoll and SSE clients
Steps to test cutover in sandbox and how to request early migration
communication_plan: Public blog and support KB with timeline and FAQs
In-product console banner and per-customer email sequences
Weekly migration status updates for customers in opt-in and canary cohorts
Support SLA credits process and a templated customer notice for billing adjustments
risks_mitigation: Risk: silent client failures —> Mitigation: strict circuit-breaker thresholds and aggressive telemetry
Risk: billing misattribution —> Mitigation: simulation run against billing test data and manual audit step
Risk: increased ops load —> Mitigation: dedicated on-call runbook and reserved engineering rotations
open_questions: How to handle third-party proxies that buffer SSE connections?
Thresholds for circuit-breaker per-org default vs. custom
Formal definition of 'migration-induced error' for billing credit eligibility
notes: Reviewed with SRE and Billing on 2026-03-10; SRE requested an additional canary gate at 10%
Finance requested manual approval step before issuing credits for any customer >$10k monthly spend
